title: Panic myth flip — aisle 7 (Meera, 36)
caption:
Myth: a panic attack means your heart is failing. Actually it's a false alarm that peaks in minutes, then falls (DSM-5-TR 2022; Klein 1993). Which myth should we flip next? 👇
www.aiforheratx.org
#panicattacks #anxietyrelief #womensmentalhealth #anxietysupport #nervoussystem #womenshealth

scenes.text: Panic peaks within minutes and then comes down — that's part of its actual definition (DSM-5-TR, 2022).
phrases: Meera, 36. Cart half full, kid waiting in the car.
Her heart went to 140 somewhere near the yogurt.
It peaked. Then, slowly, it dropped.
Panic peaks in minutes and falls — that's the definition (DSM-5-TR).

scenes.text: It wasn't her heart. Her brain misread normal CO2 as suffocating — Donald Klein named that false alarm in 1993.
phrases: You look completely fine now though.
It wasn't stress. My brain read normal CO2 as suffocating (Klein, 1993).

scenes.text: Women are diagnosed with panic disorder about twice as often as men (NIMH).
Tonight: five cyclic sighs, a 20-minute walk tomorrow, and tell a therapist about the aisle-7 one.
phrases: 1. Five cyclic sighs: two inhales in, one long slow exhale out.
2. Walk 20 minutes tomorrow — the WHO asks for 150 a week.
3. Tell a therapist about aisle 7. That is exactly what they are for.
